## 

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/data_cycle.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Data Collection Cycle**

The data collection process involves planning, collecting, processing, and analyzing data in a cyclical manner.
:::

## 

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/pftc4.JPG)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Plant Functional Trait Courses**

This presentation covers best practices for reproducible data collection in ecological research.
:::

## Design spreadsheets

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/spreadsheets.jpg)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Designing Effective Spreadsheets**

Proper spreadsheet design is crucial for data collection. Use clear column headers, consistent formatting, and validation rules.
:::

## Spreadsheet content

::: {style="font-size: 70%;"}
-   Date, time
-   Location: region/site
-   Experimental design: transect, block, plot, treatments, replicate
-   Organism: species/population/genet
-   Unique ID for sample/observation
-   Response
-   Predictors
-   METADATA: recorder/scribe, weather, notes
:::

## Design spreadsheet - paper

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/envelope.jpeg)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Paper-based Data Collection**

Traditional paper forms can be effective but require careful design and clear instructions for data entry.
:::

## Design spreadsheet - digital

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/digital.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Digital Data Collection**

Digital forms offer advantages like immediate validation, automatic calculations, and easier data transfer.
:::

## Design spreadsheet - data validation

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/typos.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Data Validation - Common Errors**

Typographical errors and inconsistencies are common in data entry. Use validation rules to prevent these issues.
:::

## Design spreadsheet - data validation

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/validation.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Data Validation Techniques**

Implement dropdown menus, range checks, and format validation to ensure data quality.
:::

## Digitizing spreadsheets

## Tidy data

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/tidydata_1.jpg)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Tidy Data Principles**

Tidy data follows three principles: each variable forms a column, each observation forms a row, and each type of observational unit forms a table.
:::

## Long or wide format

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/tidyr-pivot_wider_longer.gif)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Long vs Wide Format**

- **Long format**: Each row represents one observation, variables are in separate columns
- **Wide format**: Each row represents one subject, repeated measurements are in separate columns
- Use `pivot_longer()` to convert wide to long
- Use `pivot_wider()` to convert long to wide
:::

## Consistency in datasheets

## Consistency - meaningful names

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/final.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Meaningful Variable Names**

Choose descriptive and consistent names for variables. Avoid abbreviations and use clear, meaningful terms.
:::

## Consistency - meaningful names

::: callout-note
### Exercise

Discuss in pairs: which of these are meaningful variable names?
:::

-   T

-   bird_raw

-   jja1b

-   mean

-   data

-   ddd

## Consistency - meaningful names

-   A name can contain letters, numbers, dot and underscore

-   First letter must be letter or dot. If the first character in a name is a dot, the object is invisible.

-   Avoid special characters (e.g. æ, å, ø, ö)

-   Avoid reserved names: function, TRUE, mean, etc.

## Consistency - style

["Good coding style is like correct punctuation: you can manage without it, butitsuremakesthingseasiertoread."](https://style.tidyverse.org/)

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/cases.jpg)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Coding Style Importance**

Good coding style improves readability and maintainability. Use consistent naming conventions and formatting.
:::

## Consistent style with styler


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(styler)
 
style_text("my_function<-function(my_data){
  my_data|> group_by(group)|> 
    summarise(mean=mean(variable),se=sd(variable)/sqrt(n()))}")  
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
my_function <- function(my_data) {
  my_data |>
    group_by(group) |>
    summarise(mean = mean(variable), se = sd(variable) / sqrt(n()))
}
```


:::
:::


## Useful package for style

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/styler.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Styler Package**

The styler package automatically formats R code according to tidyverse style guidelines.
:::

## Consistency - standards

Use global data standards (ISO) when available for dates: yyyy-mm-dd

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](pics/dates.png)
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Date Standards**

Use ISO format (yyyy-mm-dd) for dates to ensure consistency and avoid ambiguity across different systems.
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
